title: Diffraction limit of a circular aperture at 550 nm
caption: The smallest resolvable angle is θ = 1.22λ/D, which falls as the aperture grows: smaller apertures give wider patterns. For the 3 mm pupil, θ = 1.22 × 550 nm/3 mm = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ rad = 0.8′, close to the eye's actual acuity of about 1′ (dotted).
alt: Graph of the diffraction-limited angle in minutes of arc against aperture diameter in millimetres: a falling curve through 0.8 arcminutes at 3 millimetres, with the eye's 1 arcminute acuity marked.
description: The horizontal axis is the aperture diameter D in millimetres; the vertical axis is the smallest resolvable angle in minutes of arc.
The curve is θ = 1.22λ/D for λ = 550 nm: it is inversely proportional to D.
At D = 3 mm (the pupil) θ = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ rad = 0.8′.
A dotted line marks the eye's actual acuity, about 1′, a little above the diffraction limit.
